explain.say: Imagine old fairy lights where one bulb blows and the whole string goes dark. Annoying! That happens because the bulbs are in series, which means joined one after another in a single loop. Let us look inside.

faq.a: Voltage, or potential difference, is the push from the battery. It tells you how much energy each unit of charge carries.
asks: What does the battery voltage mean?

faq.q: How is voltage shared in a series circuit?
faq.a: The battery voltage is split between the components. The voltages across them add up to the battery voltage.

faq.q: What happens if one bulb in series breaks?
faq.a: The single loop is broken, so no current can flow and every bulb goes out.
asks: Why do all the lights go out in series?

faq.q: Is current the same everywhere in a series circuit?
faq.a: Yes. There is only one path, so the same current flows through every part.

faq.q: Why do bulbs in series get dimmer when you add more?
faq.a: Each extra bulb adds resistance and takes a share of the voltage, so the current falls and each bulb gets less energy.

facts: In a series circuit, the current is the same at every point.
In series, the potential differences across components add up to the supply voltage.

wrong.1: In series the voltage is shared, not given in full to each.
wrong.2: The bulbs cannot get more than the battery supplies.
